 Top 3 AI Chip Stocks To Watch In October 2026
 October 17, 2026 SI Simply Wall St Reviewed by Sasha Jovanovic AI spending is now important enough that the Federal Reserve is openly talking about a possible AI shock to the economy. That kind of focus pulls serious capital into the chips, factories and equipment powering all this computing. Investors who ignore the hardware backbone risk missing a significant part of the story. This article discusses three stocks from our screener that tap directly into that build out.
 The stocks covered below are only a small sample of what sits inside the broader semiconductor supply chain universe, and the full screen surfaced 48 more hardware focused companies with equally compelling narratives that are not discussed here. To go straight to the source and identify your own highest conviction angles across equipment makers, foundries and chip designers, analyze the Semiconductor Supply Chain screener .
 Advertisement Applied Materials (AMAT)
 Overview: Applied Materials supplies chipmaking equipment, services, and software that manufacturers use to build and fine tune advanced semiconductor wafers and devices for AI workloads.
 Operations: The business generates about US$22.4b from Semiconductor Systems and US$7.2b from Applied Global Services, with sizeable sales across China, Taiwan, Korea, and the United States.
 Market Cap: US$341.3b
 Applied Materials matters for this screener because its tools sit directly on the factory floor where AI accelerators, memory, and packaging capacity are being built out, and management is now leaning into higher value parts of that production chain.
 "The mix shift toward leading edge foundry logic, DRAM including high bandwidth memory, and advanced packaging is expected to account for most wafer fab equipment growth in 2026 and 2027, and Applied Materials is forecasting more than 70% growth in advanced packaging revenue and more than 50% growth in process diagnostics and control in 2026. Applied Global Services is expected to grow more than 20% in calendar 2026 with a long term target in the mid teens, supported by more than 37,000 connected chambers using AI enabled diagnostics that can more than double revenue per tool under new contracts in some cases." 
 What ultimately happens to future margins and cash generation will hinge on how one quiet shift in its product and service mix plays out.
 That quiet shift is the real story. Read the full narrative for Applied Materials to see how mix, contracts, and AI driven services could be reshaping Applied Materials future earnings power.
 NasdaqGS:AMAT Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026 Sandisk (SNDK)
 Overview: Sandisk develops NAND flash based solid state drives and embedded storage that power data centers, cloud platforms, AI servers, and a broad range of devices.
 Operations: Sandisk generates US$20.2b from data storage devices and solutions, with major revenue from Hong Kong, China, the rest of Asia, the United States, and EMEA.
 Market Cap: US$204.2b
 Sandisk matters for this Semiconductor Supply Chain screener because its NAND based SSDs and embedded flash give AI infrastructure the storage capacity and speed needed to keep massive models fed with data.
 "Rapid AI and cloud workload expansion is associated with data center NAND exabyte growth outpacing overall supply. This environment supports Sandisk's enterprise SSD portfolio and its deepening hyperscaler engagements, which in turn support its revenue and pricing power." 
 The key issue now is how the evolving balance between tight supply and long term AI storage commitments ultimately shapes margins and cash generation.
 That supply demand tension is just the start, and the full narrative for Sandisk maps how AI storage commitments, pricing cycles, and capital intensity could be reshaping Sandisk's risk reward profile.
 NasdaqGS:SNDK Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026 Technoprobe (BIT:TPRO)
 Overview: Technoprobe designs and manufactures probe cards and interfaces that let chipmakers electrically test advanced AI, data center and 5G semiconductors.
 Operations: Technoprobe generates about €766.6 million from semiconductor equipment and services, with most sales in Asia and America, and smaller contributions from Italy and wider Europe.
 Market Cap: €17.0b
 Technoprobe matters here because its probe cards sit in the test phase of the AI supply chain, where every wafer must be checked before those chips head into data centers, cars or connected devices.
 "If this AI test cycle continues over several years, the share price could rise as the company converts this volume into higher revenue and earnings." 
 The key factor now is how a shift in test complexity and content per device could affect long-term margins.
 That shift in test content is already reshaping the story. The full narrative for Technoprobe shows how rising complexity and AI demand could accelerate Technoprobe's earnings power.

 2 | 0 RU RudolfdeLeeuw on Micron Technology · 2 days ago The contracted-volume angle is the strongest part of this thesis, since 16 agreements covering about 20% of DRAM volume gives some floor under pricing. What I would watch is the capex response: with margins this high, DRAM and HBM supply additions from Samsung, SK Hynix and the Chinese players typically arrive 4 to 6 quarters later. I would frame valuation on through-cycle earnings rather than peak EPS, and track HBM share at Nvidia's next platform and contract pricing resets as the key signals of whether this cycle is really structural.
